title: Pricing a Prescription at the Counter on a Ridgecrest RxSecure Plan
content:
What a member of a Ridgecrest RxSecure stand-alone Medicare Part D prescription drug plan pays at the counter is chosen by the formulary tier the product sits on, the standing of the dispensing pharmacy and the payment stage the member is in. The one-month figure applied is the figure the per-tier cost-share schedule gives for the fill's formulary tier at that pharmacy's network standing.

A fill is priced only while the enrollment is in force or in its premium grace period on the fill date of the prescription.

## How the figure is chosen

1. A preferred retail pharmacy gives the plan's preferred figure and a standard retail pharmacy its standard figure.
2. The member never pays more than the negotiated price however the multiplier falls.
3. A covered insulin product costs the member no more than the insulin cap for a one-month supply, whatever tier it sits on and whatever stage the member is in, and the deductible is never taken on insulin.
4. Adult vaccines recommended by the immunisation schedule cost the member nothing at any stage.
5. Where CMS has told the plan that the member has the full low-income subsidy, the subsidy copays replace the plan's own figures and the plan's deductible does not apply.

## Authorisation and network standing

Where the fill's formulary tier is one the plan held enforces prior authorisation on, an approved coverage determination covering that product and still inside its approved through date is on record.

A fill at an out-of-network pharmacy is handled on the footing the out-of-network rule of the plan held gives, and where it is covered only in an emergency the member pays the pharmacy and claims the difference back from the plan.

A fill rejected at the counter is never simply refused: the member is told the reason code, what the plan needs, and that they may ask for a coverage determination the same day.

## Clauses no longer in force

The following clauses of this policy are **no longer in force** and are set out here only so that they are not applied:

1. "What the member pays at the counter is taken from the negotiated price for the product" — no longer in force.
2. "mail order and ninety-day retail fills take the one-month figure multiplied by the tier's extended-supply multiplier" — no longer in force.
